title: Twilight ops brief — anomalous model-serving tail latency and GPU node churn
summary: Night window (00:30-04:30 UTC) had an intermittent p95/p99 tail latency spike for hosted text-generation routes and transient GPU node churn in eu-west-1. Impact: increased error retries for some customers and elevated token cost due to retries. Root cause likely combination of a noisy model variant causing longer KV-cache churn and a kernel-level OOM on a single NVIDIA host that triggered kubelet pod restarts.
timeline:
00:32 UTC — Alert triggered: route /v1/generate p95 > 1200ms (baseline ~180ms).
00:37 UTC — Initial paging to SRE rotation.
00:45 UTC — Observed spike correlated with model 'open-zh-medium-v2' traffic (canary traffic + small customer burst).
00:53 UTC — GPU host gpu-node-eu-7 reported kernel OOMs and pod evictions; pods rescheduled across remaining nodes.
01:02 UTC — Autoscaling kicked in (nodepool scale up request), but new nodes provisioning lagged (~9m).
01:11 UTC — We temporarily diverted 20% of traffic to eu-central-1 using smart routing policy; p95 improved to ~250ms.
01:25 UTC — Rolled back 'open-zh-medium-v2' to previous quantized variant for canary traffic (rollback id: rollout-2026-03-24-01).
01:40 UTC — Error rate (5xx) normalized back to baseline; retries decreased.
02:05 UTC — Verified system health; continuing monitoring during handoff.
actions_taken:
- Identified affected model variant by correlating model_id tags with request traces (trace IDs example: 01f3a...).
- Rolled back canary variant and enforced quantized variant for remaining traffic.
- Re-routed 20% traffic to eu-central-1 via smart-routing policy to relieve eu-west-1 pressure.
- Manually cordoned gpu-node-eu-7 and provisioned replacement node (nodepool autoscaler request SCL-174).
- Applied temporary alert suppression for noisy transient kernel OOM alerts to avoid alert fatigue (suppression window 00:58-01:20 UTC).
- Opened a kernel-level debug session with infra (ticket SRE-342) to get dmesg/stack traces from gpu-node-eu-7.
- Added a short-term traffic cap on the affected canary deployment to avoid cascading slowdowns.
outstanding_followups:
- Root cause analysis: infra to collect full kernel logs and GPU driver dumps from gpu-node-eu-7 (owner: Marcus Blake, due: 2026-03-27).
- Post-incident tuning for autoscaler: reduce node provisioning latency by pre-warming images in eu-west nodepool (owner: Lina Chen, due: 2026-04-02).
- Update model onboarding checklist to include KV-cache pressure test for canary traffic patterns (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-31).
- Create synthetic workload to reproduce p99 tail from persisted KV churn (owner: Ethan Morales, due: 2026-03-29).
- Revisit alert thresholds: set separate alert for model-induced latency vs infra-induced latency (owner: SRE alerting working group, due: 2026-04-06).
escalations:
- Level 2: Eng-infra paged for kernel OOM analysis at 00:55 UTC (escalated to L2).
- Level 3: Not required; incident stabilized before infra L3 intervention.
- Customer comms: CS alerted two affected midsize customers at 01:20 UTC with mitigation summary and ETA for RCA. (CS contact: Maya Rodriguez)
metrics_snapshot:
00:30-01:30 UTC window:
- p50: 120ms (baseline 100–180ms depending on route).
- p95: peaked 1250ms -> stabilized 240ms after routing/rollback.
- p99: peaked 2.8s -> 700ms after mitigation.
- 5xx rate: baseline 0.02% -> peaked 1.8% during spike.
- gpu-node-eu-7: GPU memory usage 98% at spike, kernel OOMs recorded.
- nodepool available capacity: 2 spare nodes before incident, provisioning lag ~9m.
notes_to_next_rotation:
- Watch for recurring kernel OOMs on eu-west-1 hosts; if popping again, escalate to infra L3 immediately and apply traffic diversion earlier.
- If p95 > 400ms for >5min, temporarily reduce canary traffic to 0% for that model by default.
- Reference rollout-2026-03-24-01 in handoff if follow-up required.
- Please attach any extra traces to SRE-342 and add final RCA link when complete.
freeform_notes:
Quick observations: the KV cache churn pattern suggests the canary may be triggering longer attention spans resulting in larger KV growth; the quantized variant reduced memory pressure noticeably. Consider adding a lightweight KV size estimate metric to the serving trace to catch this earlier. Also, provisioning hit a cold-image delay — nodeprewarm seems high ROI for this customer mix.
Unresolved question: did a recent kernel/driver patch deploy to eu-west nodepool between 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-23? Infra to confirm.
